info.title: Edgrapi — US Government Data API
info.description: Official US government data as clean JSON on one API key. SEC EDGAR filings (insider Form 4 trades, 8-K events, 13F fund holdings, 13D/13G activist stakes, financial statements and ratios), SAM.gov federal contract opportunities, USAspending awards, Grants.gov grant opportunities, and US House Congress stock trades. Hosted MCP server plus REST, with real-time webhooks when a watched company files. One key, one normalized schema.

post.summary: How to get an API key
post.description:
Anonymous key minting is disabled. Each anonymous mint created a fresh 50-credit account,
so the free tier was bypassable by key rotation (a scripted client could get unlimited free
access). Getting a key now requires a free account — email, no card — which keeps one wallet
per person and preserves the paywall. Existing keys keep working; the dashboard mints more.

get.description:
Company profile from SEC EDGAR: name, CIK, SIC industry, exchanges, fiscal
year end. The lookup you make before any other call.

get.summary: Financial statements (income, balance sheet, cash flow)
get.description:
Income statement, balance sheet, and cash flow from SEC filings as clean
JSON, annual or quarterly. Same field names for every company, so you stop
writing per-ticker special cases.

14 named ratios worked out from a company's SEC statements: margins, ROE,
ROA, current ratio, debt-to-equity, and revenue growth. Also returns the
per-share figures (eps_diluted, book_value_per_share, shares_outstanding) so
you can compute price ratios yourself: P/E = your price / eps_diluted,
P/B = your price / book_value_per_share.

Every filing a company has made, each linked to the document on SEC.gov.
Filter by form to pull just the 10-Ks, the 8-Ks, or the Form 4s.

Narrative sections from the latest 10-K/10-Q as clean text (Risk Factors,
MD&A, Business, etc.) — built for LLM/RAG equity research.

get.summary: Download a filing document by accession
get.description:
Fetch a filing's document straight from the EDGAR archive, through Edgrapi's
politeness gate, circuit breaker and week-long cache, so you don't hit SEC.gov
directly or manage the User-Agent and rate limits. Omit `file` to get the primary
document (the 10-K, 8-K, Form 4, etc.); pass `file` to pull a specific exhibit.
Text documents (HTML, XML, TXT) only; binary exhibits keep their SEC.gov URL in
/v1/filings.

get.description:
Parsed insider transactions from SEC Form 4 (and 3/5): who traded, their
role, the transaction code, share count, price, and whether the trade was an
open-market decision or automatic compensation. Code P (open-market purchase)
is the only signal where the insider spent their own money; sales tagged
plan_10b5_1 were pre-scheduled and carry little signal.

Use ticker='latest' for the market-wide feed of the biggest open-market insider
BUYS, or ticker='clusters' for companies where several insiders bought at once
(the cluster-buy signal), newest and largest first.

get.summary: Form 144 — notices of proposed insider sales
get.description:
Form 144 notices — an insider's declared INTENT to sell restricted or control
stock, filed before the sale executes and shows up on a Form 4. A leading
intent-to-sell signal, parsed: the seller, their relationship to the issuer, and
each security block (shares to be sold, aggregate market value, approximate sale
date, exchange, broker), with totals across the notice.

schema.description: Recent notices to return; higher = slower on a cold ticker (one SEC fetch per notice)

get.description:
A fund's latest 13F portfolio, parsed from the SEC information table, ranked by
value, and diffed against the prior quarter so every position is labelled new,
added, reduced or unchanged — with the exits listed separately.

Positions are aggregated by CUSIP (funds split one holding across sub-managers, so
the raw table double-counts). Options carry a `put_call` flag: a PUT is a bearish
bet, not a long, and reporting it as a holding is the classic 13F mistake. Value is
whole dollars. Each position also carries a best-effort `ticker` resolved from its
CUSIP; the issuer name and CUSIP stay authoritative, and `ticker` is null when the
CUSIP has no US equity listing (a bond, a foreign issue) or isn't resolved yet.

Identify the fund by a known name (berkshire, burry, ackman, bridgewater, citadel,
…), a raw CIK, or a ticker when the manager is itself public (BRK-B). 13F is a
quarterly snapshot filed up to 45 days after quarter-end — it is a lagged position
report, not a live trade feed.

parameters.name: identifier

schema.description: Fund name (e.g. 'berkshire', 'burry', 'pershing-square'), a CIK, or a ticker whose company is the filer (e.g. BRK-B)
schema.title: Identifier

parameters.description: Fund name (e.g. 'berkshire', 'burry', 'pershing-square'), a CIK, or a ticker whose company is the filer (e.g. BRK-B)

get.description:
Schedule 13D and 13G filings — the disclosure anyone crossing 5% of a company's
voting stock must make. A 13D signals possible activist intent (board pushes, sales,
strategy); a 13G is a passive large holder. The `/A` suffix is an amendment (stake
raised, trimmed, or intent changed). Each record carries the issuer, CUSIP, the
reporting person(s), and the exact percent of class, parsed from the SEC's structured
13D/G XML.

Use identifier='latest' for the real-time market-wide feed of new >5% stakes (the
activist radar), or a ticker to list the 13D/13G filings indexed on that company. The
per-company view reads an accumulating store, so it deepens as the feed runs — it is a
rolling recent window, not the full historical record.

parameters.name: identifier

schema.description: 'latest' for the market-wide 13D/13G feed, or a ticker to list stakes indexed on that company

get.description:
Market-wide feed of recent 8-K item 4.02 filings — non-reliance on previously
issued financial statements, i.e. a company announcing its past financials can no
longer be trusted. One of the strongest red-flag signals in the filings.

Market-wide feed of recent 8-K item 4.01 filings — changes in the registrant's
certifying accountant (an auditor switch). A resignation or dismissal of the auditor
is a governance red flag worth watching.

8-K material events for a company as a typed stream: each event carries its
item codes with human labels (2.02 earnings, 5.02 exec change, 1.05 cyber
incident...), a `notable` flag for the market-moving ones, and a link to the
filing. Set notable=true to skip routine 8-Ks, or item=4.02 to pull just one
event type (e.g. every restatement this company has filed).

get.summary: Resolve a ticker, CIK, or CUSIP to a company
get.description:
Map any one of ticker / CIK / CUSIP to the canonical SEC entity: legal name,
CIK, ticker(s), exchange, SIC industry and sector, state of incorporation, and
business location. The foundational lookup the other endpoints lean on. CUSIP
resolution goes through the same crosswalk 13F holdings use, so a CUSIP with no
US-listed equity (bonds, delisted, foreign) returns 404.

Search the full text of every SEC filing since 2001, the same index behind
EDGAR full-text search. Returns the matching filing documents with company, form,
date, 8-K item codes, and a link to the document on SEC.gov. Filter by form and
date range; page with `offset`.

get.summary: All XBRL concepts reported in one filing
get.description:
Every XBRL concept value reported in a single filing, matched on the accession
number. Reconstructs one filing's structured data — each concept with its tag,
label, unit, value, and period.

Convert a company's full SEC XBRL (companyfacts) to JSON. By default returns the
normalized income statement, balance sheet and cash flow across every reported
period, plus a `concepts_index` of every us-gaap/dei tag the filer reports. Pass
`concept=` to pull the raw time series for any specific tag(s) — the complete
converter, not just the curated fundamentals.

Common shares outstanding and public float from the XBRL cover-page tags.
Shares outstanding updates every 10-Q/10-K; public float is reported on the 10-K
cover, so it refreshes about yearly. The two numbers you need for market-cap and
free-float math (multiply shares by a price from your own feed).

get.summary: Market-wide recent Form D private placements
get.description:
Recent Form D filings across all issuers — the live feed of new private
placements (Reg D raises). Each notice is parsed: issuer, jurisdiction, industry,
the amount offered and sold, the exemption claimed, and the related persons. A
funding signal that lands the day the raise is disclosed.

issuers are usually private companies, so identify them by CIK; a ticker also works

and sold, the Reg D exemption, related persons, and the date of first sale.

sources-sought, and award notices — normalized into flat JSON. Each record carries
the notice id, title, solicitation number, posted date, type, set-aside, NAICS, place
of performance, award (when present), a point of contact, and the sam.gov link. SAM
caps a query window at one year; leave the dates off for the recent feed.

Federal spending awards from USAspending.gov — contracts, grants, loans, and
direct payments — normalized into flat JSON. Each record carries the award id,
recipient, amount, awarding agency, type, dates, place of performance, description,
and the usaspending.gov link. Pick one category per call; leave dates off for the
last year. Pairs with /v1/opportunities: a solicitation on SAM, the awards on here.

get.description:
Federal grant funding opportunities from Grants.gov, normalized into flat JSON.
Each record carries the opportunity id and number, title, agency, status, the open
and close dates, the Assistance Listing (CFDA) numbers, and the grants.gov link.
Defaults to open opportunities (posted + forecasted). Completes the gov-funding
trio with /v1/opportunities (contracts) and /v1/awards (spending).

schema.description: Pipe/comma list of forecasted, posted, closed, archived (default posted|forecasted)

get.description:
Recent congressional stock trades, newest first, parsed from US House STOCK Act
periodic transaction reports. Each record carries the member, state/district, ticker,
buy or sell, the disclosed dollar range, the transaction and disclosure dates, and a link
to the House disclosure PDF. House-only for now; the Senate feed is coming.

Congressional stock trades in one ticker, newest first, from US House STOCK Act
periodic transaction reports. Same fields as the feed: member, buy/sell, dollar range,
dates, and the House disclosure PDF link. House-only for now.

The company's subsidiaries and their jurisdictions of incorporation, parsed from
Exhibit 21 of its latest 10-K. Exhibit 21 is an HTML exhibit whose layout varies by
filer, so this is a best-effort table parse; the list is empty (free) when a filer
files no Exhibit 21, which is common for companies claiming the significant-subsidiary
exemption.

get.description: List your webhooks (secrets are not returned).

post.description:
Register a webhook. Body: {"url": "https://...", "tickers": ["AAPL","MSFT"],
"events": ["insider","8-k"]}. You get a signing secret back, shown once.

url.description: https:// endpoint that receives the signed POSTs

events.description: Event types to fire on (default: insider, 8-k)

delete.description:
Permanently delete a webhook you own. Returns 404 if no webhook with that id exists
for your account (rather than falsely reporting success for an unknown id).

post.description:
Send a signed test payload to a webhook so you can verify your endpoint
and signature check before a real filing arrives.

get.summary: Recent delivery attempts for a webhook
get.description:
The recent delivery attempts for a webhook you own: the event, ticker, accession, whether the
POST succeeded, the HTTP status, and any error. The audit trail for debugging your endpoint.
